subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Peak-bagging challenges and traverse challenges are two approaches to organized mountaineering goals.
• Peak-bagging challenges focus on summiting every mountain on a defined list, regardless of the route taken between them.
• Such a challenge based on the Colorado Fourteeners might involve Jabari Sow climbing all 58 peaks in the state that exceed 14,000 feet, traveling by car between trailheads.
• Traverse challenges focus on completing a continuous route across a mountain range on foot, linking peaks and passes without returning to a trailhead.
• Such a challenge based on California's Sierra High Route might involve Viktor Dubois walking 195 miles of mostly off-trail terrain from Kings Canyon to Yosemite in a single push.
prompt: The student wants to present traverse challenges to an audience unfamiliar with the concept. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: An approach to organized mountaineering, traverse challenges focus on completing a continuous route across a mountain range on foot, linking peaks and passes without returning to a trailhead.
choices.B: Peak-bagging challenges focus on summiting every mountain on a defined list, regardless of the route taken between them.
choices.C: A challenge based on California's Sierra High Route might involve walking 195 miles of mostly off-trail terrain from Kings Canyon to Yosemite in a single push.
choices.D: Traverse challenges differ from peak-bagging challenges in that peak-bagging challenges focus on summiting every mountain on a defined list.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence effectively presents traverse challenges to an audience unfamiliar with the concept, identifying it as an approach to organized mountaineering and explaining that it focuses on completing a continuous on-foot route across a mountain range, linking peaks and passes without returning to a trailhead.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The sentence provides an example of a traverse challenge in practice but doesn't explain what traverse challenges are; it thus doesn't effectively present the concept to an unfamiliar audience.
